quotes.text: You can build perfect orchestration around terrible data and you'll still produce hallucinations but you can't build perfect data and survive without orchestration.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames data governance and orchestration as complementary, non-optional layers against hallucinations.

quotes.text: Retrieval governance controls what the model can see but orchestration controls what the model can do. It's the difference between limiting what goes in and limiting what comes out both are mandatory.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp distinction between input-side and output-side controls in AI architecture.

quotes.text: Every permission you were too busy to revoke is now part of the AI's brain. Every site you added someone to, but forgot to clean up, is now part of their search results.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the impact of permission sprawl on Copilot retrieval tangible.

quotes.text: A model cannot lie with confidence if it is forced to show its work with citations. It cannot make up stories if it isn't allowed to make claims without proof.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes why grounding must be a hard constraint rather than a feature.

quotes.text: Being helpful without being accurate is a huge liability for a company. Being accurate without being helpful might feel incomplete, but it is much easier to defend.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core trade-off behind designing prompts and guardrails for enterprise AI.

takeaways: Copilot hallucinations stem mostly from orchestration, retrieval and data-quality choices, not from the language model alone.
Permission sprawl, unlabeled content and stale documents turn Microsoft 365 into a source of confident but wrong answers.
Retrieval-first governance, grounding as a hard constraint, validation gates and golden-dataset regression testing keep Copilot reliable over time.
hook: Your Copilot gives fluent, cited answers that are quietly wrong, and everyone blames the model. This deep dive for Microsoft 365 architects and governance teams shows how retrieval, permissions, prompts and governance theatre build a hallucination machine, and which controls dismantle it.
